answer: No: the disclosure does not support underwriting positive jaws in FY26. The >$500m productivity target looks mainly like an offset to continuing wage, banker and UNITE pressure, albeit a larger offset than FY25, rather than a net cost-out promise. FY25 net operating income grew 3% while operating expenses grew 9%, or 6% excluding restructuring. Its expense bridge shows $402m of productivity against larger combined staff, technology, volume/other and investment pressure. For FY26, Westpac targets >$500m productivity but also flags a 3%-to-4% EBA increase, banker investment and higher UNITE spend. UNITE rises from $660m in FY25, 74% expensed, to $850m-$950m in FY26, about 75% expensed; the plan remains investment-heavy through FY27-FY28 and extends into FY29. Reductions in non-UNITE investment help, but without FY26 income or total expense guidance, positive jaws cannot be established.

key_facts.fact: FY25 net operating income was $22,464m, up 3%, while operating expenses were $11,916m, up 9%; expenses rose 6% excluding restructuring.

citations.quote: Excluding these costs, operating expenses increased 6% mainly due to higher staff costs and the step up in UNITE investment spend.

key_facts.fact: The FY25 expense bridge ran from $10,944m to $11,916m, with $397m staff, $146m technology, $199m volume/other and $359m investment pressure, offset by $402m productivity, before a $273m restructuring charge.

citations.quote: Staff costs Technology Volume and other Productivity Investments Restructuring charge

key_facts.fact: Westpac targets more than $500m of FY26 productivity while flagging a 3%-to-4% EBA increase, banker investment and increased UNITE spend.

citations.quote: EBA increase 3% to 4% and investment in bankers
Fit for Growth benefits to contribute to targeted productivity of >$500m in FY26

key_facts.fact: FY25 investment spend was $1,918m: 34% UNITE, 30% growth and productivity, and 36% risk and regulatory; UNITE spend was $660m with 74% expensed.

citations.quote: UNITE accounted for 34%, growth and productivity initiatives accounted for 30% and 36% was directed towards risk and regulatory activities.
UNITE investment spend increased to $660 million with 74% expensed.

key_facts.fact: UNITE investment is expected to be $850m-$950m in FY26 with about 75% expensed; the plan extends into FY29 and UNITE is about 40% of total investment spend in FY27-FY28.

key_facts.fact: Westpac expects total FY26 investment spend of about $2bn, with reductions in both growth/productivity and risk/regulatory spend.

citations.quote: Expect reductions in both growth & productivity and risk & regulation spend

limitations: Westpac does not disclose FY26 revenue growth or total expense growth, so positive jaws cannot be demonstrated.
The dollar reduction in FY26 growth/productivity and risk/regulatory investment is not disclosed.
The disclosure does not separate gross, recurring and in-year productivity benefits.
No UNITE-specific amortisation period is disclosed; the 2.7-year figure is the average for all capitalised software.
